title: Number of Ways to Select Buildings
summary: Given a 0-indexed binary string s representing the types of buildings along a street, where '0' denotes an office and '1' denotes a restaurant, determine the number of valid ways to select 3 buildings such that no two consecutive buildings are of the same type.
statement: Given a 0-indexed binary string s representing the types of buildings along a street, where '0' denotes an office and '1' denotes a restaurant, determine the number of valid ways to select 3 buildings such that no two consecutive buildings are of the same type.
constraints: Choose exactly three indices in strictly increasing order.
The selected types must be 010 or 101; adjacency in the original street is not required.
Return the number of index triples, counting equal type patterns at different positions separately.
hints: Every valid triple is determined by its middle building.
For a zero center, multiply ones before it by ones after it; do the symmetric calculation for a one center.
Track left counts during one scan and derive right counts from global totals.
Each valid triple has one unique middle index, so summing the independent choices on its two sides counts every valid selection exactly once.
editorial: Each valid triple has one unique middle index, so summing the independent choices on its two sides counts every valid selection exactly once.

tests.explanation: Four selections form 010 and two form 101, giving six valid triples.
There is no zero between two ones and no one between two zeros, so the result is zero.
